Class HtmlSimulation

java.lang.Object
com.eco.bio7.spatial.HtmlSimulation
public class HtmlSimulation extends Object
Exports an interactive simulation to an HTML page (a single file without dependencies, WebGL for 3D): Play/Pause, Step, Reset, the speed and controls for the settings (sliders, number fields, text fields, check boxes, choices and buttons) with a 2D grid view (e.g., a cellular automaton), a 3D view (e.g., agents of a swarm model) or a dynamic 3D surface and an optional chart of values over time.

The simulation runs in the web browser: the model is written in JavaScript with the functions setup(sim) (called at the start and with Reset) and step(sim) (one time step). The settings are available as sim.p.name. The view displays (an optional function draw(sim) is called after the view is drawn):

  • GRID_2D: sim.cells (an array of sim.width * sim.height values, index y * width + x) with sim.palette (colors of the integer states, e.g., ['#ffffff', '#000000']) or the color map (or the colors of sim.ramp) with sim.min and sim.max and optional agents sim.agents = {x: [], y: [], color: '#d62728', radius: 0.5} (cell units).
  • SCENE_3D: sim.box = [w, h, d] and sim.points = {xyz: [x0, y0, z0, x1, ...], colors: [r, g, b, ...] (0 - 1, optional), color: '#1f77b4', radius: 0.01} and sim.lines = {xyz: [...], color: '#555555'} (pairs of points).
  • SURFACE_3D: sim.surface = {nx, ny, z: [...] (index i * ny + j), min, max} colored with the color map (and points and lines like SCENE_3D).
sim.chart('Name', value) adds a value to a series of the chart (one value per step), sim.clearChart() removes the values. sim.t is the number of the steps, sim.random() a random number and sim.pause() pauses the simulation (step(sim) can also return false to stop without counting the step, or 'stop' to stop after the step). An optional (async) function prepare(sim) is called once before the start (e.g., to load data).

Example: 

new HtmlSimulation("Game of Life").view(HtmlSimulation.View.GRID_2D).slider("density", "Start density", 0, 1, 0.01, 0.3)
                .number("size", "Grid size", 100).restartOn("size", "density").chart("Population").code(js).export("/path/life.html");

    • asynchronous

      public HtmlSimulation asynchronous(boolean asynchronous)

    • inputs

      public HtmlSimulation inputs(Collection<String> events)
      The input of the view for the model: "click", "drag" and/or "key". The page calls the function input(sim, ev) of the code with ev = {type: 'click', x, y} (a grid: cells, x and y from the top left; the 3D view: the point on the floor), {type: 'drag', x, y} (the 2D view: a drag, the 3D view: Shift + drag) or {type: 'key', key} (the key of the keyboard event). Default: none.

    • autoplay

      public HtmlSimulation autoplay(boolean autoplay)
      Starts the simulation when the page is opened (default false).

    • layout

      public HtmlSimulation layout(String layout)
      The layout of the page: "classic" (a sidebar with the controls, the default), "dashboard" (a top bar with Play/Pause, the view, the settings on the right), "focus" (the view fills the window, floating panels which can be hidden) or "story" (one column: the title, the view, the controls, the settings in a grid, the chart). All layouts adapt to narrow windows (phones).

    • accent

      public HtmlSimulation accent(String accent)
      The accent color of the page: "blue" (default), "teal", "violet", "orange" or "graphite".

    • theme

      public HtmlSimulation theme(String theme)
      The theme of the page: "auto" (the light or dark setting of the system, the default), "light" or "dark". The page has a button to change it.

    • scene

      public HtmlSimulation scene(String background, String lighting, String shape, String floor, boolean shadows)
      The look of the 3D views (SCENE_3D, SURFACE_3D). The page has a "View" panel to change it (see sceneControls).
      Parameters:
      background - "auto" (studio or night as the theme), "studio", "night", "sky", "sunset", "ocean", "paper" or "plain"
      lighting - "studio", "soft", "dramatic" or "flat"
      shape - the shape of the points: "sphere", "cube", "cone", "glider" (cones and gliders point in the direction of the movement) or "point" (fast point sprites)
      floor - "grid", "plane" or "none"
      shadows - soft shadows of the points on the floor

    • map

      public HtmlSimulation map(double south, double west, double north, double east, String basemap, double opacity, String attribution)
      Shows the 2D grid on a map (online base maps with Leaflet): the grid covers the geographic bounds (WGS84 degrees; the grid is drawn in Web Mercator, exact for a grid in EPSG:3857). NaN bounds: the map shows sim.mapBounds of the model (e.g., agents with sim.geoAgents = {lon, lat, colors, sizes, labels}). The page has a "Map" panel (the base map, the opacity, the map on or off). Colors with an alpha (#rrggbbaa) show the map.
      Parameters:
      basemap - "topo" (OpenTopoMap, CC-BY-SA) or "osm" (OpenStreetMap: only for a page on a web server, its tile servers block a local file); both need no key and show their attribution
      opacity - the opacity of the grid (0 - 1)
      attribution - the source of the data (shown on the map), e.g., "Terrain Tiles"
